commits.edited_message:
Use sliding window for lossless internal pixel buffers

Replace full-height dec->pixels allocations with a sliding row
window bounded by the maximum VP8L backward-reference distance
and copy length.

The window is sized to exactly the number of rows that must stay
resident between two consecutive ShiftWindow() calls, capped to the
image height.

Change-Id: I399190a7c195abc2c506ea53febca5db770a317f
(cherry picked from commit e7a9045111cfb6349affc37e64d6664f5f77dc93)

use sliding window for decoded alpha rows

Allocate only a sliding output row window for dec->alpha_plane in
AllocateMemory (frame_dec.c) when alpha dithering is not active.

The window keeps the single previous row that ALPHDecode() carries
across calls (alph_dec->prev_line), which is also the row consumed by
spatial unfiltering and fancy upsampling.

Change-Id: I2a32c3ed493f6e097e573cf5cf0de8a9c96fcfae
(cherry picked from commit bb3ad5bc2440c28c5006f99d81d051460210d261)

coupling:
Heap out-of-bounds WRITE in the alpha sliding-window output buffer (dec->alpha_plane), overflowed by WebPUnfilters[] in ALPHDecode() while decoding the last macroblock row of a lossy WebP that carries an uncompressed alpha plane (ALPHA_NO_COMPRESSION) with strong/complex loop filtering. The buffer holds num_output_rows = WebPGetAlphaWindowRows(), and its write bound is enforced only by that row count.

The defect requires BOTH edits together:
  * Commit 44e809983e... (lossless sliding window) introduces the shared sizing helper VP8LGetWindowRows(). Its edit drops the 2x amortization factor, so the helper now returns exactly min_rows = max_history_rows + NUM_ARGB_CACHE_ROWS + max_length_rows + 2. Read alone this is correct: min_rows is the true per-shift minimum (the 2x was only a memmove-amortization margin), so the lossless dec->pixels window it sizes stays safe, and the alpha window it sizes (still max_history_rows=25) stays >= the 25 rows the alpha decoder needs.
  * Commit 9c0929e06a... (alpha sliding window) is the only caller that passes max_history_rows for alpha. Its edit lowers that argument from 25 to 1, justified by the fact that ALPHDecode() carries only a single history row (prev_line) across calls. Read alone this is also safe: with the 2x factor still present the helper returns 2*(1+16+max_length_rows+2), which is still well above the 25 rows needed (and, for the PoC's 32-row image, is >= height, so the window degenerates to full height and never slides).

Only with BOTH edits does WebPGetAlphaWindowRows() collapse to 1+NUM_ARGB_CACHE_ROWS+max_length_rows+2 = 21 rows (< 25 needed, and < the 32-row image height so sliding is active). On the final macroblock row the alpha decoder shifts the window to keep prev_line (output_start_row = row-1) and then unfilters 24 rows at window offset 1, i.e. rows [1,25) into a 21-row buffer -> 4-row heap overflow.

The fix is non-local: neither commit's diff is wrong on its own. Restoring max_history_rows for alpha requires knowing it feeds a helper whose amortization slack was removed in the other commit, and the real invariant (window >= max rows ALPHDecode writes per call, ~25) is never named in either single diff. A reviewer must reason across both commits and across two files (frame_dec.c sizes the buffer, alpha_dec.c writes it) to see that the composed row count underflows the per-call write span.
